reviews.title: He spared no expense
reviews.text: A truly wonderful app. I’ve had quite a few attempts at sobriety and Drynosaur is the most enjoyable tool I’ve found in my attempts.

reviews.title: It’s not just the Drynosaur
reviews.text:
I wanted an app to help with not just my drinking, but a distraction from drinking. 
The creator included a mini game that is similar to Tetris, which has proven to help people with PTSD and stress. 
I tend to drink because I have both of those things prevalent in my life. 

The app is designed fairly minimal, with daily check ins and opportunities to earn widgets for your phone, games to play for currency in the game and you also get to watch your Dino grow through sobriety!

reviews.title: Love it BUT
reviews.text:
I think this is a phenomenal idea and is implemented wonderfully, I only wish there was a way to record previous sobriety, i just downloaded today but I have almost 2 years and would like if the app reflected that.

Amending because the creator quickly got back to me to show me that the app already has this feature. Huge props to a solo dev out here doing more work than entire organizations of people. You rock man keep it up.

reviews.title: Love!
reviews.text: Drynosaur is the only alcohol tracking app I’ve actually been able to stick with and use nearly every day - I’ve used my earned coins to buy some widgets so I use it more frequently now that I can see it on my Home Screen. I like the daily check-ins and feeds. The information is really helpful and it’s just so cute - reminds me of my Giga pets or Tamagotchi’s as a kid.

reviews.title: Excellent
reviews.text: I found this app very helpful and cute. Also the games that allow you to get the coins for the widgets is very helpful.

reviews.title: $9.99 a WEEK? Hell naw.
reviews.text: It’s a great concept and honestly would be a helpful tool, but $40 a month is bananas! Kind of a shame to be honest.

reviews.title: Cute, comforting and engaging

reviews.title: Helped me get sober
reviews.text: I was having a problem with multiple different substances and vices for years. I'd occasionally having a couple months kinda clean from just white knuckling. I found this app randomly on instagram & instantly downloaded it. It helped immensely for the first two weeks then I started going to NA to continue to support my recovery. I'm currently living in sober living (which I love!), have an amazing group of sober friends and almost at 5 months clean. I just got a second drynosaur in the game that I'm specifically going to use for my adult entertainment addiction that I want to kick. I never leave reviews for anything, but this app was the catalyst that changed my life immensely. The differences are day and night!! I can't recommend this enough & I tell all my friends wanting to get sober about this app:) Thank you, Gareth!!

reviews.title: Oh so its not free
reviews.text: Why not just charge to download the app or say theres no free version before i download and get started and then find out i have to pay a subscription. Also, the very first question it asks you is, “do you drink often?”, and then only option is to say yes. Huh? Lol seems like itd be a nice fun sober tracker but wish there was a free version or was more clear about there not being one.

reviews.title: Waste of time until they obligate you to pay for it
reviews.text:
Basically they could just say that EVERY FEATURE is paid on the app. 
But instead of advertising it on the beginning, they make a bunch of questions about your habits and goals, then make you create a pet (choose between 3 basics dinosaurs and name it)... then you gotta pay 5$ per week or 20$ per year. No free features at all. They are just like all the others moneysuckers apps who just want your money and that's all. 
There's way better apps to help you keep sober and its for free, so go search for it... otherwise just keep drinking instead of wasting money on it lol

reviews.title: People struggling can't get through a pay wall.
reviews.text: Stop pretending it's a free app. To hit a paywall after kinda getting excited about it is lame. I'll watch ads.

reviews.title: Not a good start
reviews.text: Seemed like a fun way to track the sober days. Getting started was an inconvenience. Asking questions and only giving you one option as an answer seems redundant. Then the cost to continue seemed to be a little expensive for what it is.

reviews.title: Do NOT waste your money on this app!!!
reviews.text:
- What do you like?
Really not all that sure what I like about it. It seemed a lot cooler or interactive than it actually is. Especially for the cost for even a year. There are 100's of sobriety clocks, timers, calendars and calculators out there that are free and have ALOT more substance to them I'm very dissatisfied and sure do feel like I not only wasted money, but that whomever is leaving such positive reviews have done the same. 

- What could be better?
Pretty much everything. Maybe AA or recovery tools and or info. Motivational content. AlANYTHING REALLY. All this does is say how many days you "check in" and didn't drink the previous day or since last checked in. Such a waste. 


- Any feature ideas?
Don't charge for an app that is beyond basic. Maybe be free or suggest people go to better sobriety apps? There are some really great feee ones out there both AA and non AA related

I hope this review finds you BEFORE downloading. It will force you to buy not even a trial period. It's a huge waste of money. It's got 3 basic games that any old Nokia phone had. And 3 "mindfulness" activities that are as basic as they come. Save your time and money there are much better FREE apps out there to support you in sobriety!!!!

reviews.title: Eh
reviews.text: I love the idea with this app & was really looking forward to using it, but per usual it costs money, $40 a year? $25 a year with current discount? Would love to use this app, but there’s so many helpful & free resources/apps out there 🤷‍♂️

reviews.title: Paywall after ~4 days
reviews.text: This app is supposed to be about helping you stay sober instead they send you 3 notifications to pay them before you can even try the app, then 4 days later it won't let you close the paywall without paying. Server costs will be right around .50$ per year per user. Make that money with ads, but asking 30$ then downplaying it by saying "it's less than a night out" is downright insulting to the user. Prey on people that can afford it, but doing it to someone who is struggling with alcohol is downright disgusting.
